acceptance.given: Package A unit, boundary, negative, and CLI integration cases are selected by the repository-owned pytest terminal selection with explicit case/assertion mappings.

oracle.expected: The pytest result and case/assertion mapping expose one independently evaluated expected-result assertion for every executed Package A case, including negative fixtures that pass when rejected as expected.
forbidden: Any required case is missing, skipped, deselected, xfailed, zero-case, or ends in a harness error while the selection is treated as passing
A negative fixture rejected as expected is counted as an overall suite failure
oracle.observable: pytest terminal output and the repository-owned case/assertion mapping can be inspected after the selection completes

acceptance.then: Every executed Package A case has its own expected-result outcome and the terminal selection reports the mapped results without accepting missing or harness-invalid required cases.
acceptance.when: After the repository-owned pytest terminal selection completes, evaluate each selected case and its explicit case/assertion mapping.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the repository-owned Package A pytest terminal selection with a case whose expected-result assertion or explicit case/assertion mapping is absent; the selector must fail rather than report the case as independently evaluated.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure the Package A terminal selection records and exposes an independent expected-result assertion and mapping for every executed case, while preserving required-case and negative-fixture outcome semantics.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema change; revert only the Package A case-result evaluation logic and retain existing selector compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Selected Package A cases transition from terminal execution to individually evaluated expected-result outcomes with explicit mappings.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The repository-owned Package A pytest selection completes with a non-empty, complete case/assertion mapping and an independently observable expected-result outcome for every required case; missing, skipped, deselected, xfailed, zero-case, or harness-error required cases prevent success.
